The first meeting of the Twentieth Session of the National Assembly commenced at 14:03 hours under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Chairperson Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable members, the proceedings of today's meeting of the National Assembly commence. Honourable members, I heartily welcome all the Honourable members present at the first meeting of the Twentieth Session of the Assembly.
Honourable members, a letter has been received from the Right Honourable President regarding the convening of the session. Now, I will inform you of the contents of the said letter.
Right Honourable Chairperson,
National Assembly,
Singha Durbar, Kathmandu.
In accordance with Article 93, Sub-section (1) of the Constitution of Nepal, I have convened the session of the Federal Parliament, comprising both houses, on Thursday, Chaitra 19, 2082 BS, at 14:00 hours, based on the recommendation of the Government of Nepal, Council of Ministers, dated Chaitra 16, 2082 BS.
(Padma Prasad Pandey)
Secretary General
(Ram Chandra Poudel)
President
Chaitra 16, 2082
Honourable members, let us now observe one minute of silence standing in tribute to the unknown martyrs who sacrificed their lives for the cause of democracy.
Honourable members, I heartily welcome all the Honourable members on the occasion of the commencement of the 20th Session of the Federal Parliament, National Assembly. The National Assembly, which began on Falgun 21, 2074 BS, has already completed 19 sessions in 8 years. During this period, due to the active role of the Honourable members, the National Assembly has succeeded in presenting a dignified image of a mature, understanding, coordinated, cooperative, and stable assembly. For this, I express my highest respect to the Honourable members and praise your role.
As the National Assembly is a permanent house, constitutional provisions stipulate that one-third of the members' terms expire every two years and elections are held accordingly. We bid farewell to 19 members in Falgun and have formally welcomed 18 newly elected members. I once again heartily welcome the newly elected Honourable members to the National Assembly meeting.
Honourable members, we conducted the 19th session from Magh 4 to Falgun 1, 2082 BS, amidst the 'Gen-Z' movement and subsequent political developments. Although it was a short session in terms of time, I feel that the 19th session was significant and dignified in terms of responsibility and work. We have completed important tasks through the National Assembly amidst a kind of uncertainty due to the changed political situation of the country after the Gen-Z movement and the dissolution of the House of Representatives and the announcement of new elections. We have been able to resolve some legal complexities and, by reaching consensus, cooperation, and coordination with the government, the Federal Parliament, political parties, and other stakeholders, we have been able to build mutual trust in accordance with the spirit of the constitution and provide an exemplary role in dispelling the fear and uncertainty generated among the public. I feel the National Assembly is proud of this.
Honourable members, by the time the 19th session of the National Assembly concluded and the 20th session commenced, there has been a significant change in the country's political landscape. The Nepali people have given a new mandate through the general elections to the House of Representatives concluded on Falgun 21. Accordingly, the Rastriya Swatantra Party has secured a single majority, and a new government has been formed under the leadership of the Right Honourable Prime Minister Pushpa Kamal Dahal.
In a democratic system, the mandate expressed through the people's vote is supreme, and it is essential for the parliament and the entire state machinery to be accountable to that mandate. The public expects the new government to bring speed to good governance, transparency, accountability, effectiveness of service delivery, and development works. It is our shared responsibility to provide appropriate direction to the government through policies, laws, and oversight to address such aspirations and expectations of the public. In this regard, I believe the role of the National Assembly will also be equally important. Furthermore, we are all confident that the government will function lawfully and respect the public sentiment.
Honourable members, the interrelationship, cooperation, and coexistence between the two houses of the Federal Parliament, the House of Representatives and the National Assembly, are the basis of democratic parliamentary practice. While the House of Representatives is the house of representatives elected by the direct vote of the people, the National Assembly symbolizes the balance, continuity, and mature deliberation of the federal structure. If the environment of mutual coordination, respect, and cooperation between these two houses is strengthened, the overall effectiveness of the parliament will further increase. Therefore, I express my belief that constructive cooperation, experience sharing, and coordination between both houses will be further strengthened in the coming days.
Honourable members, due to the damage to the Federal Parliament building in Baneshwor and the under-construction new parliament building in Singha Durbar not yet being fully completed, we have been compelled to conduct the assembly facing challenging circumstances for some time. We are in a situation where we have to conduct this session from this very assembly hall.
(Padma Prasad Pandey)
Secretary General
We all expect that the assembly and parliamentary activities will be facilitated once the under-construction parliament building is completed soon. Furthermore, the use of modern technology in the new building will help make the parliament's work more organized, transparent, and effective. I express hope that parliamentary work will be further strengthened through the use of digital systems, archiving, information flow, and innovative technologies for conducting meetings.
Honourable members, I believe that the experience and contribution of the newly elected Honourable members who have come as members of the National Assembly from this session onwards will further enrich the work of the National Assembly. The Federal Parliament Secretariat is preparing an orientation program for the newly elected members with the objective of providing information regarding parliamentary practice, legislative process, roles of committees, and parliamentary etiquette.
I expect this to help make parliamentary work more organized and effective. I believe that the Honourable members will participate actively, constructively, and accountably in the bills, policy matters, and national and provincial concerns to be discussed in this assembly in the coming days. The beauty of democratic practice lies in the culture of moving forward based on healthy debate, diversity of opinions, and consensus. Therefore, like in past sessions, I also expect that the opinions presented here will be respectful, fact-based, and focused on the welfare of the people.
The parliament plays a very important role in directing the overall development of the country in the right direction through the government's policies and laws and in improving the living standards of the people. In particular, the National Assembly has been making a significant contribution by meticulously studying and refining bills and providing necessary suggestions from the perspective of long-term national interest. I expect that the National Assembly will effectively fulfill its constitutional duties and responsibilities in this session as well. Our common objective is the welfare, prosperity, and good governance of the people of the country. To achieve this goal, it is necessary today to rise above political differences and prioritize national interest.
(Padma Prasad Pandey)
Secretary General
Therefore, I also heartily appeal to the Honourable members to play a dignified, responsible, and positive role in the parliament. Expressing my belief that the active cooperation and effective role of all Honourable members will be instrumental in effectively conducting the National Assembly, I extend my best wishes for the complete success of the 20th session.
Honourable members, in the context of the commencement of the Twentieth Session of the National Assembly, names have been presented to deliver their remarks on behalf of the parties represented in the National Assembly. I will now provide time sequentially to the Honourable members. First, Honourable Member Krishna Prasad Sitaula.

I am a worker of such a party, Congress, we took up arms in the revolution of 2007, the Rana regime ended. But the same last ruler, Mohan Shamsher, became the Prime Minister and the late revered leader of this country, B.P. Koirala, became the Home Minister. We never believe in politics of revenge. If we all, all political parties of the country, move forward unitedly without the spirit of revenge, without the spirit of retribution, only then will this country be built. Unity is not for us, not for power, not for power sharing, but for the people, to build a common point in policy making so that the nation can be moved forward by everyone together. There is the problem of employment, the problem of unemployment, many people have aspirations. How many lakhs of people are in the Gulf countries, war is happening there. Our brothers and sisters living in distress, what will be the condition of those people? If we all think seriously and create a new policy, then we can address that issue. How much has our economy shrunk, what is our economic situation, how much budget will come, we all know this. But in all these matters, with our broad unity and understanding, the nation can be built, the country can move forward. Similarly, the world politics of today is not the same as it was 4 years ago. The bombing of Iran by America, Ukraine and Russia, the Gulf countries, the whole world is in a state of panic. Our Nepalis, whether they are in any part of Europe, whether they are soldiers recruited in Russia, whether they are people in Ukraine, whether they are people in the Gulf countries, whether they have reached Iran, even people who have reached America, people who have suffered due to America's changed policies, if we do not all stand together as Nepalis and build a new map for the country within this constitution, then a new kind of conflict can arise in Nepal again. The outside world thinks Nepal is always like this, but we should not feel sad for Nepal. The suffering of the people, the happiness of the people, the prosperity of the people is a matter of our common effort. I just want to say this much, I want to give special best wishes to the government, that the government can work extensively for the benefit of the people, for building national unity, in strengthening the constitution, in correctly implementing the contents of the constitution. There is support for the good work done by the government, and opposition for wrong work. Therefore, as I said at the beginning, it would be happy if there was never a situation where we had to oppose the government. With this wish, I conclude my remarks, honorable chairperson. Finally, I just want to say this much. This country is for all of us. Terai, hills, mountains, Mechi, Mahakali, people of all classes, regions, all religions, all cultures, if anyone walks around with arrogance, with ego, with pride, saying I have this large number, then somewhere they will stumble, somewhere they will get hurt. Therefore, the government must always walk with open eyes, with an open mind, with openness. We have fallen into destruction many times due to the ego of 'only what I do is right', we ourselves have fallen. Let that not happen now, let us all sit together and engage in the campaign of nation building. With this wish, let K.P. Oli, Ramesh Lekhak be released soon, let the people get justice soon. (14:51 hrs) Honorable Ms. Puja Chaudhary (Janata Samajwadi Party Nepal): Honorable Chairperson, I would like to extend my heartfelt congratulations and best wishes for a successful term from my party, JSP Nepal, and on my own behalf to all the honorable members of the National Assembly and the House of Representatives who have just been elected with the people's trust. I also extend my warm congratulations to the youth of our country, the new Prime Minister, and all the members of the cabinet. Honorable members, the Twentieth Session of the Federal Parliament, National Assembly, commenced on Thursday, Chaitra 19, 2082, at 2:00 PM and continued for a total of 9 days until Friday, Chaitra 27, 2082. During this period, 5 meetings were held, and a total of 5 hours and 44 minutes were spent on assembly work. Today, the address by the Honorable President to the joint session of both houses was also completed.

During this session, there were Zero Hour sessions in 3 meetings. During that time, 26 Honorable members utilized 26 minutes, while there was a Special Time session in 1 meeting. During the Special Time, 12 Honorable members utilized 1 hour and 27 minutes. During this period, the assembly welcomed one-third newly elected Honorable members. Honorable members, with the objective of providing information on parliamentary practices, legislative procedures, the role of committees, and parliamentary tenure, the Federal Parliament Secretariat is preparing an orientation program for newly elected members. The Chairperson of the House is scheduled to depart on April 1st for the 152nd Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) General Assembly to be held in Istanbul, Turkey, from May 15th to 19th, 2083, along with two honorable members. Formal information regarding the orientation program will be provided to the honorable members upon their return from the IPU.

Honorable Prem Prasad Dahal proposed Honorable Lila Kumari Bhandari for the position, detailing her extensive political background, including her involvement in student movements, the Maoist insurgency, Constituent Assembly roles, and her position within the CPN (UML). He emphasized her qualifications and the consensus reached among parties for her candidacy.

They criticize a government decision restricting advertisements in private media as undemocratic and a threat to press freedom. The speaker also raises concerns about increasing cyberbullying against adolescent girls and urges the government to take strict action and effectively implement cybercrime prevention measures.

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Honorable Member Samjhana Devkota spoke about the government's undemocratic decisions and praised the 33% women's representation in the cabinet. Honorable Member Mohammad Khalid raised concerns about the illegal arrest of KP Sharma Oli, the plight of Nepali workers in Saudi Arabia, the security of Nepalis in the Middle East due to the Iran-Israel war, rising fuel prices, and difficulties in gas cylinder exchange. He also highlighted the issue of cyberbullying against women and children and called for stricter laws and support for the Cyber Bureau. Honorable Member Tul Prasad Bishwakarma congratulated the newly elected Vice-President and committee chairs, praised the Rastriya Swatantra Party's electoral success, and advised the government to seek consensus. He also spoke about the global impact of the Middle East conflict, rising inflation, and the need for government action. Honorable Member Narayan Dutt Bhatt discussed the undeclared world war in the Middle East, condemning US actions against Iran and expressing solidarity with the Iranian people. He noted the global and national impact of the war, including rising prices and oil shortages, and urged the government to take timely action.
